text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Glencor International and a Belgian, company Union Minier, are the two bidders for 58 percent of the Pirdop copper smelter to have submitted offers in the Privatisation Agency by the April 24 deadline.
-- Heating rates rise 18 percent from May 1, under a decision of the Energy Ministry to generate sufficient revenue to cover operation costs.
-- Defense minister Georgi Ananiev said he will launch investigations aimed to curb corruption in the higher echelons of his ministry in an operation dubbed Moscuito.

-- Workers laid off in closing state loss-making enterprises should receive $1,000 in severance payments from an extended World Bank loan to unable them to start small businesses, said Social Wellfare Minister Ivan Neikov. They now receive $250.
-- 160 people suffered injuries, mostly due to alcoholic intoxication, during the Orthodox Easter holidays, the emergency hospital said.

-- Cement Francaise warned in a letter Bulgarian authorities to investigate inconsistencies in the Devnia cement plant sell-off deal about to be completed between Marvex, a Spanish-Bulgarian joint venture and Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency.
-- Bulgaria and Romania agreed to combine efforts in fighting the mafia during the visit of Romanian President Emil Constantinescu on Wednesday.

-- Bulgarian customs authorities have seized 120 kg of heroin worth some $12 million at the Capitan Andreevo border check point with Turkey in the past three months. The drugs are expected to be burned shortly. -- Sofia Newsroom, ++359-2-9814145
